items.title: collect mining: coerce plain {x,y,z} pool entries to Vec3 before b.blockAt (fix 'pos.floored is not a function')
items.target_gap: Worker mining cards dead-end: '[zee] [collect] Error mining oak_log at -159,74,-262: pos.floored is not a function [x4] [card:t_864e056d]' -> SUPPLY/gather work cannot complete.
evidence: In-game: zee repeatedly failed to mine oak_log; 4 consecutive 'pos.floored is not a function' errors on one card.

Root cause: ordering.js trunk-harvest branch (clusters -> orderCells) and all-same-y volume branch both map candidates through orderCells -> normalizeUnit ({...c, id}), which yields PLAIN {x,y,z} objects (no Vec3 prototype). state.pool = sorted.slice() feeds these straight into round 1. mineflayer's b.blockAt(point) calls point.floored() internally, so a plain object throws.

Instrumented test confirmed: first 5 candidates from `sorted` arrive as plain Object (floored=undefined); only refreshPool() candidates (raw b.findBlocks) are Vec3. The harvest loop CATCHES the per-candidate throw and recovers via refreshPool, so mined_count can still hit target on dense patches -- masking the bug -- but trunk/sparse harvests keep throwing on every `sorted` candidate (the [x4] the operator saw).

files: bot/lib/actions/mining/collect/execute.js: import { Vec3 }; in processCandidate, coerce `pos` to Vec3 at the single chokepoint before any b.blockAt/pos.offset/distanceTo/GoalNear use. Mirrors the reactive.js Vec3-guard pattern.

bot/test/actions/mining-collect.test.js: regression test with a blockAt stub that mimics mineflayer (requires .floored()); asserts no candidate logs 'pos.floored is not a function'. Fails pre-fix (reproduces exact error string), passes post-fix.

expected_metrics.note: Same-arm validation signal: oak_log/trunk SUPPLY cards complete instead of dead-ending; board_quality.cards no longer shows repeated collect dig_failed on a single trunk card. No 'pos.floored' in action logs.

items.title: schematic shelter bootstrap: speak the real hermes kanban CLI (create/body-trailer-epic/link), not add/--for/--after/edit --body
items.target_gap: The schematic starter_shelter workflow (the feature the operator asked to exercise) NEVER files a single card: maybe_bootstrap_schematic_shelter_for_run raises every poller cycle ('[poller] shelter render failed: kanban failed: usage: hermes kanban ...'). schematic_shelter_bootstrapped never set -> retries forever; the run is effectively plain emergent, not schematic.
evidence: gv2-2026-06-24-2 poller.log: '[poller] shelter render failed: kanban failed: usage: hermes kanban [-h] [--board <slug>] {init,boards,create,...}' repeated every cycle (~30+ min).

Root cause: file_starter_shelter_sequence (scripts/lib/gv2_schematic_shelter.py) was authored against a CLI that does not exist. Real `hermes kanban` has verb `create` (not `add`); has NO --for / --after flags; `create` accepts only --parent; `edit` takes --result, NOT --body (so the create-'pending'-then-edit-body two-step could never set a body).

Verified against live CLI: `hermes kanban create --help` (only --parent), `hermes kanban edit --help` (--result/--summary/--metadata, no --body). Sibling scripts/construct-plan-cards.py has the same imaginary-CLI bug (shells scripts/kanban facade which uses create/--epic/--depends-on) — left for a follow-up; not in the poller hot path.

Facade scripts/kanban shows the correct semantics: --epic = membership via body trailer (---\nepic: <id>), NOT a link; --depends-on = prereq via `hermes kanban link <parent> <child>`. Using --parent to an [EPIC] card causes the epic-parent deadlock this project already hit (project_genesis_v2_decomp_gaps).
